To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the microbial community of deeply buried marine shallow shelf sediments off New Jersey, U.S.A., is dominated by Bacteria, with the bacterial candidate division JS-1 and the classes Caldilineae and Anaerolineae of the phylum Chloroflexi being almost as highly abundant.
the deeply buried marine sedimets of the shallow shelf of the New Jersey continental margin are inhabited by a diverse and complex microbial community.
the deeply buried marine sedimets of the New Jersey shelf are characterized by a low organic carbon content, low total cell counts, and low dsrA gene abundance, but high Fe(III) reducer abundance.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the characterization of a microbial community in deeply buried marine sediment that was deposited in the late Cretaceous to early Eocene, and that has not been exposed to the surface for millions of years.
the diversity and abundance of the sedimentary microbial community and its potential to degrade organic compounds and to oxidize reduced compounds in the deeply buried marine sedimets.
the identification and quantification of the dominant microbial groups and their functional genes in deeply buried sediments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the investigated deeply buried sediments of the shelf off New Jersey are characterized by the presence of the typical deep subsurface microbial community, but with a high abundance of the candidate division JS1.

the investigated deeply buried marine shelf sediments of New Jersey, USA are inhabited by a diverse and abundant community of Archaea and Bacteri, which is dominated by the classes Anaerolinaceae and Caldilineae of the phylum Chloroflexi, the candidate division JS1, sulfate reducers, and the Fe(III)/Mn(IV) reducers of the family Geobacteraceae.
the investigated sediments of the shelf of New Jersey are characterized by a low organic carbon input and a low microbial activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the microbial community in the investigated deeply buried marine shelf sediments is composed of typical deep subsurface microbial groups, which are adapted to a low energy input, and a high diversity of uncultured microorganisms.
the investigated sediments of the NJ shelf are inhabited by a microbial community of low cell numbers, but with a high diversity.
the microbial communities in deeply buried sediments of the continental shelf off New Jersey are characterized by low cell numbers and low diversity of the isolated bacterial 16S rRNAs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
deeply buried sediments of the marine shelf off New Jersey are dominated by Bacteria, which are mainly represented by the candidate division JS1.
the microbial community of the investigated deeply buried marine sediment of the shallow shelf was dominated by Bacteria, but the Archaea were not negligible.

the deeply buried marine sedimets are inhabited by a microbial community with low cell counts and a low organic carbon content, which is dominated by Bacteria, and the Bacteria are dominated by the phylum Chloroflexi.
